rationale: Consistency fix in the knowledge record. The statement about which entry points the proposal gate covers now exists twice: the original entry recorded it as source-derived and explicitly not executed, and a second entry created in the previous batch carries the same statement with the read-index receipt. The original entry is corrected to point at that executed evidence, so no reviewer reads a stale claim that the boundary was never observed. No interpretation used the original entry, so no use needs re-evaluating.

knowledge.statement: The proposal gate covers the MsgProp entry points of the Node API and nothing else. node.Propose, node.ProposeConfChange and node.Step with a MsgProp all end in stepWithWaitOption, which sends on n.propc, the channel the run loop only receives from while its gate variable is armed; every other message type, including MsgReadIndex, is sent on n.recvc instead. A member whose gate is disarmed therefore has its proposals and configuration proposals held, while its other duties - forwarding read-index requests to the leader it knows, answering messages and participating in replication and application - are not routed through the gate.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop in this snapshot, whichever configuration flags are used, with the run loop's gate variable disarmed for the local member; the boundary is now backed by a retained read-index control on a re-added member (read state observed, proposal held), in addition to the source anchors.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier conditions said the statement was source-derived and had not been executed as a control. A read-index control was executed afterwards and is now cited, so the conditions no longer claim the boundary is unobserved. The statement itself is unchanged; a second entry carrying the same statement with the receipt also exists, and either can be cited.
